1. (Currently Amended) A method for restoring efficiency of a photovoltaic cell, the method comprising: illuminating a photovoltaic cell such that the photovoltaic cell receives a time integrated irradiance __measured in units equivalent to peak solar irradiance__ of at least 5 hours of solar illumination; and annealing the photovoltaic cell at a temperature above 90 degrees Celsius for a minimum of 10 minutes, the annealing performed in response to illuminating the photovoltaic cell.

2. (Currently Amended) The method of Claim 1, wherein the photovoltaic cell comprises a semiconductor wafer, and wherein __the method further comprises one of the following:__ the photovoltaic cell receives a time integrated irradiance equivalent to at least 20 hours of solar illumination; __the photovoltaic cell receives a time integrated irradiance equivalent to at least 16 hours of solar illumination, and the photovoltaic cell is heated to at least 50 degrees Celsius during the illuminating step;__ and __the photovoltaic cell is irradiated in sunlight using a solar concentrator for at least 10 hours, wherein the solar concentrator increases the irradiance of solar illumination on the photovoltaic cell by a factor of 2 to 5, and the photovoltaic cell is annealed at a temperature above 90 degrees Celsius for a minimum of 10 minutes following such irradiation.__.

3. (Currently Amended) The method of Claim 2, wherein the photovoltaic cell is annealed at a temperature above 130 degrees Celsius, and wherein __the method further comprises__ illuminating the photovoltaic cell __during the annealing step__.

4. (Currently Amended) The method of Claim 3, wherein illuminating the photovoltaic cell during annealing of the photovoltaic cell is performed such that the photovoltaic cell receives a time integrated irradiance equivalent to at least 10 minutes of solar illumination.

5. (Previously presented) The method of Claim 1, wherein the semiconductor wafer is a silicon semiconductor wafer.

6. (Previously presented) The method of Claim 1, wherein the photovoltaic cell is annealed at a temperature between 140 degrees Celsius and 210 degrees Celsius for a minimum of 2 hours.

7. (Previously presented) The method of Claim 6, wherein the photovoltaic cell is a thin film photovoltaic cell.

8. (Previously presented) The method of Claim 6, wherein the photovoltaic cell is an amorphous silicon thin film photovoltaic cell.

9. (Previously presented) The method of claim 1, wherein the photovoltaic cell is illuminated after manufacturing of the photovoltaic cell is complete such that the photovoltaic cell produces electricity when illuminated.

10. (Previously presented) The method of claim 1, wherein the photovoltaic cell is illuminated with a light source that simulates light from the sun.
